q: 1. The intercept between a given arch and a linear arch at a section is proportional to
options: the shear force at the section
the vertical reaction at the support
the bending moment at the section
explain: The vertical distance (intercept) between an actual arch axis and the linear (funicular/thrust-line) arch at any section is proportional to the bending moment at that section (M = H×intercept).

q: 2. The reaction locus a two hinged parabolic arch is
options: a horizontal line parallel to the span
explain: As a point load moves across a two-hinged parabolic arch, the locus of resultant reaction traces a parabolic curve.

q: 3. The maximum tension in a cable occurs
options: at the highest point in the cable
at the lowest point in the cable
at the center of the cable
at all points in the cable
explain: In a suspended cable, tension is a combination of horizontal component (constant) and vertical component (varying with slope); it is maximum at the supports (highest points), where the cable's slope is steepest.

q: 4. A parabolic cable is subjected to a rise of t°C in temperature. Then the increase in dip of the cable is proportional to
explain: The extra length gained due to thermal expansion relates to dip change through a relation involving the square of the span, giving increase in dip proportional to (span)².

q: 5. A three hinged girder is used to stiffen a cable of a suspension bridge. Then the bending moment in the girder due to loads will be
explain: In an ideal stiffened suspension system with a three-hinged girder matching the cable's thrust line, the girder carries zero bending moment throughout, all load being carried by cable tension.

q: 6. A cable subjected to udl over its entire span assumes a shape of
explain: A cable under a uniformly distributed load (per unit horizontal length, like a suspension bridge deck) takes the shape of a parabola.

q: 7. Which of the following methods of structure analysis is a force method?
explain: Column Analogy and Method of Consistent Deformation are Force Methods (Flexibility Methods), where redundant forces are the unknowns. Slope Deflection and Moment Distribution are Displacement Methods.

q: 8. Degree of static indeterminacy of the frame is equal to (refer to image 1666)
explain: Calculated using $D_s = 3c - r'$, where 'c' is the number of closed loops and 'r' represents the releases at supports or hinges.

q: 9. Portal method of framed analysis for horizontal loads is appropriate for a frame:
options: that has a width greater than its height
that has a height greater than its width
explain: The portal method is an approximate method suitable for low-rise frames where the width is significant relative to the height.

q: 10. The effective length of a column with both ends fixed is
explain: For a column fixed at both ends, the effective length is Le = L/2, per Euler's standard end-condition factors.

q: 11. Which of the following structural analysis is a force method?
explain: Column analogy treats the redundants as forces, making it a force-based method.

q: 12. Stiffness factor is calculated in structural members for analyzing it by
explain: The moment distribution method relies heavily on member stiffness to distribute unbalanced moments.

q: 13. The effective length of a column with one end fixed and the other end hinged is
explain: For a column fixed at one end and hinged at the other, the effective length is Le = L/√2.

q: 14. In the case of long columns the maximum permissible stress depends on
options: the ultimate crushing strength of the material
explain: For long columns, buckling (governed by slenderness ratio, combining both length and radius of gyration) controls failure, so permissible stress depends on the maximum slenderness ratio.

q: 15. Unequal settlement in the supports of statically indeterminate structure develop
explain: Settlement in indeterminate structures induces internal forces and reactions that wouldn't exist in a determinate structure.

q: 16. The moment distribution method is best suited for
explain: as per key 1 MDM is specifically designed for rigid frames and continuous beams where joint rotations occur.

q: 17. In the moment distribution method, the sum of distribution factors of all the members meeting at any joint is always :
explain: The total unbalanced moment must be 100% distributed, so $\sum DF = 1$.

q: 18. The stiffness method in structural analysis is also known as :
explain: The stiffness method uses displacements as the primary unknowns, hence it is a displacement method.

q: 19. In the Euler's theory for long columns it is assumed that
options: the failure occurs by crushing of the material
the failure occurs by buckling only
the column shortens so much that it will become a short column
the column is having initial curvature and the load is eccentrically applied
explain: Euler's column theory is based purely on elastic instability (buckling) failure, ignoring crushing/direct stress effects, applicable to long columns.

q: 20. Euler's formulae for columns can be used if the slenderness ratio is
explain: Euler's formula is valid for long columns with high slenderness ratio, generally taken as greater than about 120, where buckling (not crushing) governs failure.

q: 21. What is principle of virtual work?
options: work done by external forces > internal forces
work done by external forces < internal forces
work done by external forces = work done by internal forces
explain: For a system in equilibrium, the virtual work done by external forces equals the virtual work done by internal forces.

q: 22. The statically indeterminate structures can be solved by
options: ignoring all deformations and assuming the structure to be rigid
using the equations of static and the necessary number of equations of compatibility
explain: Statically indeterminate structures require both the equilibrium (static) equations and additional compatibility equations (based on deformation) to be solved fully.

q: 23. The equations of compatibility are based on
options: the geometry of the deformed structure under the action of several forces acting
explain: Compatibility equations ensure that displacements/deformations throughout a structure remain geometrically consistent (continuous) under the applied loading.

q: 24. A dam is a
explain: A dam has all three dimensions (length, height, and thickness/width) of comparable significant magnitude, making it a three-dimensional structure.

q: 25. An internally indeterminate structure
options: may be unstable structure based on supports
explain: Internal indeterminacy (redundant members) is independent of external support conditions; depending on the supports provided, the overall structure may even be unstable.

q: 26. A concentrated load P is supported by the free end of a quadrantal ring AB whose end B is fixed. The ratio of the vertical to horizontal deflections of the end A is
explain: For a quadrant ring under an end load, applying Castigliano's theorem to find vertical and horizontal deflection components gives a ratio of π/2.

q: 27. A two hinged parabolic arch of span l and rise h carries a load varying from zero at the left end to w per unit run at the right end. The horizontal thrust is
explain: For a two-hinged parabolic arch under a linearly varying (triangular) load, the derived horizontal thrust expression is wl²/12h.

q: 28. In compression test, the fracture in cast in cast iron specimen would occur along
options: at right angles to the axis of specimen
explain: Cast iron, being weak in shear, typically fails in compression tests along an oblique (diagonal) plane where shear stress is maximum, rather than perpendicular to the load axis.

q: 29. The moment required to rotate the near end of a prismatic beam through a unit angle without translation, the far end being simply supported is given by
explain: The rotational stiffness of a prismatic member with the far end simply supported (pinned) is 3EI/L, a standard slope-deflection method coefficient.

q: 30. The moment required to rotate the near end of a prismatic beam through a unit angle without translation, the far end being fixed is given by
explain: The rotational stiffness of a prismatic member with the far end fixed is 4EI/L, the standard slope-deflection stiffness coefficient.

q: 31. If M is the external moment which rotates the near end of a prismatic beam without translation ( the far end being fixed), then the moment induced at the far end is
options: M/2 in same direction as M
M/2 in opposite direction as M
explain: The carry-over factor for a prismatic member with the far end fixed is 1/2, meaning half the applied moment M is carried over to the far end in the same rotational sense.

q: 32. A simply supported beam carrying a uniformly distributed load over its whole span, is propped at the centre of the span so that the beam is held to the level of the end supports. The reaction of the prop will be
explain: For a beam propped at midspan and brought level with the end supports under UDL, standard analysis gives the prop reaction as 5/8 of the total distributed load.

q: 33. The locus of reaction of a two hinged semi circular arch is
explain: As a moving load traverses a two-hinged semicircular arch, the locus of the resultant reaction at the support traces a straight line.

q: 34. A rigid jointed plane frame is stable and statically determinate ............. .
explain: For a rigid-jointed plane frame (each joint with 3 dof), the condition for stable and statically determinate structure is 3m + r = 3j.

q: 35. The number of independent equations to be satisfied for static equilibrium in a space structure is
explain: A three-dimensional (space) structure requires 6 independent equilibrium equations: 3 force equations (ΣFx, ΣFy, ΣFz) and 3 moment equations (ΣMx, ΣMy, ΣMz).

q: 36. The degree of static indeterminacy of a pin jointed space frame is given by
explain: For a pin-jointed space frame, each joint has 3 equilibrium equations (3D translation), giving static indeterminacy Ds = m + r − 3j.

q: 37. The degree of static indeterminacy of a rigid jointed space frame is given by
explain: For a rigid-jointed space frame, each member has 6 internal force components and each joint provides 6 equilibrium equations, giving static indeterminacy = 6m + r − 6j.

q: 38. The degree of kinematic indeterminacy of a pin jointed space frame is
explain: Each joint of a pin-jointed space frame has 3 possible translational displacements, so kinematic indeterminacy = 3j − r (subtracting restrained reaction components).

q: 39. The number of independent displacement components at each joint of a rigid jointed space frame is
explain: A rigid joint in 3D space can have 3 translations and 3 rotations, giving 6 independent displacement components per joint.

q: 40. The principle of virtual work can be applied to elastic system by considering the virtual work of
options: internal as well as external force
explain: The principle of virtual work for elastic systems equates the virtual work done by external forces to the virtual work (strain energy) done by internal forces, so both must be considered.

q: 41. Castigliano's first theorem is applicable
options: only when principle of superposition is valid
explain: Castigliano's first theorem, which relates partial derivatives of strain energy to displacements, is applicable specifically when the principle of superposition (linear elastic behavior) holds.

q: 42. A bar l meter long and having its area of cross section A, is subjected to a gradually applied load W. the strain energy stored in the bar is
explain: Strain energy stored in a bar under a gradually applied axial load W is U = W²L/2AE, the standard formula (area under the linear load-deformation curve).

q: 43. The ILD for horizontal thrust at the support of a three hinged arch when a concentrated load passes over the span is
options: a triangle with maximum ordinate at the center
a triangle with maximum ordinate at one of the supports
a parabola with maximum ordinate at the center
explain: As a unit load moves across a three-hinged arch, the influence line for horizontal thrust is a triangle peaking at the crown (mid-span), i.e., maximum ordinate at the center.

q: 44. A multi span continuous beam is simply supported at the two ends. One of the intermediate supports sinks with respect to other supports. Due to this settlement, the bending moment will get modified at
options: only the two supports adjacent to the one that sinks
all the supports except the two end supports
explain: Support settlement in a continuous beam affects the bending moments at all intermediate supports (due to the continuity/redundancy), but the two simply supported end supports (already zero moment) remain unaffected.

q: 45. For a two hinged arch, if one of the support settles horizontally, then the horizontal thrust .............
explain: A horizontal settlement (moving the supports apart) reduces the strain energy stored due to the thrust, effectively decreasing the induced horizontal thrust.

q: 46. In column analogy method, the area of an analogous column for a fixed beam of span L and flexural rigidity EI is taken as
explain: In the column analogy method, the analogous column's cross-sectional area is taken as L/EI, corresponding to the M/EI diagram base.

q: 47. The degree of static indeterminacy up to which column analogy method can be used is
explain: The column analogy method is practically limited to structures with static indeterminacy up to degree 3 (e.g., single-span fixed or portal frames), beyond which it becomes cumbersome.

q: 48. The deflection at any point of a perfect frame can be obtained by applying a unit load at the joint in
options: the direction in which the deflection is required
explain: The unit load method (virtual work) requires the unit load to be applied at the point and in the exact direction of the deflection being sought.

q: 49. In slope deflection equations, the deformations are considered to be caused by
options: both shear force and bending moment
explain: The slope-deflection method idealizes members as being deformed (bent) due to bending moment only, neglecting shear and axial deformations.

q: 50. The three moments equation is applicable only when
options: there is no settlement of supports
there is no discontinuity such as hinges within the span
explain: Clapeyron's three-moment theorem requires continuity of the beam (no internal hinges/discontinuities) between the spans considered, though it can handle varying EI, unequal spans, and support settlements with modified forms.
